function: Estimation of near-field THz MIMO channel: LSTM-FC network maps pilot measurements to angles and distance; path gains by LS; channel reconstructed (p. 5-7).
system: Wideband downlink THz MIMO-OFDM at 1 THz, near-field LoS; BS 64 and UE 16 antennas, 4 RF chains, UE at 3 km/h; no RIS (p. 2, 10).
method: LSTM plus FC network (D-STiCE), supervised with MSE loss on channel (p. 7); meta-learning with fine-tuning described for new environments, not evaluated (p. 10).
data_channel: Own near-field LoS THz channel model, Eq. (14); 200K/10K/10K samples; GAN data only illustrated (Fig. 8); 3GPP TR 38.900 cited for simulator, no measured data (p. 4, 9-10).
test_conditions: One simulator split 200K/10K/10K for train/validation/test; UE within 10 m at 3 km/h; SNR and pilot-ratio sweeps; meta-learning for new environments described, not tested (p. 10-11).
baselines: Non-learned: LS, LMMSE, CS-based (OMP) [28]. Learned: CNN-based [29], Transformer-based with similar complexity (p. 10).
metrics: NMSE and BER (QPSK, hard decision) versus SNR and pilot ratio; training loss; flops (p. 7, 10-11).
complexity: Flops formula in Eq. (43); Table I: D-STiCE 3.34e8 flops vs CS 4.96e8-1.30e9 and CNN 1.19e9-6.74e9 for three antenna settings (p. 7-8).
openness: none: no code or data link; synthetic data from the authors' simulator (p. 9-10).
q1_support: p. 10: "The channel samples are generated using (14)." and p. 4: "we use the block-fading near-field LoS channel model": a custom parametric model; 3GPP TR 38.900 [23] is cited for the simulator (p. 9) but the paper does not say the channel follows it, and no TR 38.901, DeepMIMO or measured data is used.
q2_support: p. 10: "we exploit the meta-learning, a special DL technique to solve new task with only a small number of training samples" is only a proposal; Section V trains and tests on one simulated setup (p. 10: "we generate 200 K, 10 K, and 10 K samples for the training, validation, and testing, respectively") and reports no test in a new environment.
q3_support: p. 10: "we use five benchmark schemes: 1) LS estimator, 2) LMMSE estimator, 3) CS-based channel estimation [28], 4) CNN-based channel estimation [29]" (plus a Transformer one), compared on NMSE and BER, p. 11: "the NMSE of D-STiCE is less than" 0.2 versus 0.4 to 0.7 for the others.
q4_support: p. 7: "we measure the complexity in terms of the number of floating point operations (flops)" and p. 8: "In Table I, we compare the computational complexities of D-STiCE, CS-based channel estimation, and CNN-based channel estimation".
q5_support: p. 9: "we use a synthetically generated training dataset in this work" from the authors' own simulator; no link to code or data is given anywhere in the paper.
notes: Included under area 2: parametric channel estimation, with the LSTM-FC network estimating the large-scale parameters (angles, distance) and LS/LMMSE giving the small-scale path gain (p. 5-7). Section IV (pp. 8-10) describes GAN-based data generation and meta-learning with fine-tuning for new environments, but the results of Section V (Figs. 10-13) evaluate neither, so q2 is 0 and the GAN data are not used for the reported curves (p. 10: channel samples come from Eq. (14)). Reference [23] is 3GPP TR 38.900, cited next to the simulator on p. 9 without saying the channel is built on it, so q1 is 0 but worth a check. Table I (p. 8) and Figs. 9-13 (pp. 10-11) were checked on the page images.
